thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Advance Modestly As Crucial Midterm Elections Get Under Way

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Advance Modestly As Crucial Midterm Elections Get Under Way
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
U.S. stocks drifted higher after the opening bell Tuesday, as traders awaited the results could set the political tone on Wall Street for at least the next two years.
How are the benchmarks performing?
The rose 35 points, or 0.1%, at 25, T495, the S&P 500 index added 6.7 points to reach 2,745, a rise of 0.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite Index rose 0.5%, or 38 points, at 7,366.
On Monday, the Dow rose 190.87 points to 25,461.70, a gain of 0.8%, and the S&P 500 added 15.25 points, or 0.6%, to end at 2,738.31. The Nasdaq Composite Index , meanwhile, fell 28.14 points, or 0.4%, to 7,328.85.
What's driving the market?
Midterm elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, are under way and the results could have implications for President Donald Trump's legislative agenda.
Check out:How traders are thinking about dollar wagers ahead of midterm elections, the Fed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-traders-are-thinking-about-dollar-wagers-ahead-of-midterm-elections-the-fed-2018-11-05)
In the final pre-election Wall Street Journal/NBC News poll released Sunday, Democrats held a 7 percentage-point lead on the question of which party should control the next Congress.
The most likely outcome of the elections is political gridlock, which has historically been a positive for investors, but may forestall expectations for infrastructure investments and further deregulation that might help lift shares of financial firms.
Meanwhile, investors were keeping one eye on crude-oil prices , a day after the Trump administration imposed fresh sanctions aimed at curtailing Iranian oil exports.
Abroad, market participants are also watching developments around U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May and her tense negotiations with the European Union to exit a longstanding pact with the trade bloc.
Read: Opinion: This is what's happened to stocks after every midterm election since World War II (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-whats-happened-to-stocks-after-every-midterm-election-since-world-war-ii-2018-11-05)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) are rising 0.5% in early trade, after closing at their lowest level since Aug. 1 and booking the worst two-day decline since Jan. 25, 2013. Reports that the iPhone maker was scaling back on production of a new XR model phone had contributed to its decline.
Shares of Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN) were in focus after reports that the retailing giant was set to pick two cities to host its second headquarters, possibly the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York and the Crystal City area of Arlington, Va., a Washington suburb. Shares of Amazon rose 0.4% out of the gate Tuesday.
Under Armour Inc.'s (UAA) stock is down 2% in early trading. A report in The Wall Street Journal said that employees received an email saying they were no longer able to expense strip-club outings (https://www.wsj.com/articles/under-armours-metoo-moment-no-more-strip-clubs-on-company-dime-1541450209).
Shares of CVS Health Corp. (CVS) are up 1.8% after the firm announced 6.7% same-store sales growth for the third-quarter on Tuesday morning.
Eli Lilly & Co.(LLY) stock is down 2.1% after the pharmaceutical manufacturer reported third-quarter profit and revenue beats (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/eli-lilly-beats-earnings-expectations-raises-guidance-2018-11-06), and raised its full-year guidance for 2018. The stock is up 27.4% year-to-date.
E.l.f. Beauty Inc. shares have rallied 16.4% Tuesday, after its Monday-evening earnings report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/elf-beauty-stock-rallies-after-company-beats-quarterly-views-tweaks-guidance-2018-11-05) showed the cosmetics company beating analysts' third-quarter projections for revenue and profits. The firm also raised its full-year guidance for 2018.
Shares of Marriott International Inc. (MAR) are tumbling 4.3% in early trade, after the company reported disappointing sales figures for the third quarter on Tuesday morning.
Mylan N.V.(MYL) stock is up more than 13.2%, after the company announced Monday evening that its profits more than doubled in the third quarter (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mylan-earnings-double-stock-gains-despite-revenue-miss-2018-11-05) from the year previous.
Shares of Avis Budget Group(CAR) are down 9.3% Tuesday morning, following a Monday-evening earnings report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/avis-budget-stock-drops-after-earnings-miss-2018-11-05) that had the company falling short of analysts expectations for third-quarter sales and earnings.
Booking Holdings Inc. (BKNG) stock is up more than 6% in early trade Tuesday, after the Priceline.com parent company reported that it beat analysts estimates for sales and profi (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/priceline-parent-companys-stock-jumps-nearly-8-after-earnings-2018-11-05)t in the third quarter.
Mosaic Company(MOS) shares are advancing 4.7%, following a third-quarter earnings report that showed the company benefiting from rising fertilizer prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mosaic-stock-jumps-after-earnings-show-benefits-of-higher-fertilizer-prices-2018-11-05).
Shares of Becton, Dickinson & Co. (BDX) were off 4.2% early Tuesday, after the company released earnings third-quarter earnings before the bell. The stock had been up close to 11% prior to the earnings report.
Archer Daniels Midland Co. (ADM) stock is up 1.5%, after the agriculture firm reported better-than-expected, third-quarter sales and earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/archer-daniels-earnings-and-revenue-rise-above-expectations-2018-11-06) Tuesday morning.
Shares of Ralph Lauren Corp.(RL) are falling more than 4.1%, even as the company reported revenue and profit beats for the third quarter on Tuesday morning (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ralph-lauren-earnings-and-sales-beat-expectations-but-shares-fall-6-2018-11-06). The stock had been up 32% year-to-date.
Read:These Lowe's stores are closing in the next three months (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-lowes-stores-are-closing-in-the-next-three-months-2018-11-05)
What data are in focus
A report on job openings for September due at 10 a.m. Eastern Time remains the only key data ahead on Tuesday.
What are analysts saying?
"Stocks still look to be able to rise further despite some minor stalling out over the past few days prior to this week's midterm elections. Looking back, yesterday proved that technology does not necessarily have to work every day for stocks to be able to log decent gains," said Mark Newton, founder of Newton Advisors in a Tuesday research note.
How are other markets trading?
Asian markets were mixed Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-ahead-of-us-midterm-elections-2018-11-05). European stocks were trading down on Monday, with the Stoxx Europe 600 falling 0.3%.
Oil prices were slightly lower, while gold was flat. The dollar was virtually unchanged.
